problem_statement:
Resetting primary key for a child model doesn't work.
Description
	
In the attached example code setting the primary key to None does not work (so that the existing object is overwritten on save()).
The most important code fragments of the bug example:
from django.db import models
class Item(models.Model):
	# uid = models.UUIDField(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4, editable=False)
	uid = models.AutoField(primary_key=True, editable=False)
	f = models.BooleanField(default=False)
	def reset(self):
		self.uid = None
		self.f = False
class Derived(Item):
	pass
class SaveTestCase(TestCase):
	def setUp(self):
		self.derived = Derived.objects.create(f=True) # create the first object
		item = Item.objects.get(pk=self.derived.pk)
		obj1 = item.derived
		obj1.reset()
		obj1.save() # the first object is overwritten
	def test_f_true(self):
		obj = Item.objects.get(pk=self.derived.pk)
		self.assertTrue(obj.f)
Django 2.1.2

reviewer_reasoning: The change replaces syncing the parent pk from the child link with clearing the parent_link, but it doesn’t re-sync the link to the newly created parent pk before inserting the child row. As shown by the failing tests (IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed on the parent_link/ptr_id), the child save still attempts to insert with the existing parent id, violating the OneToOne/PK constraint. This breaks parent-child syncing and doesn’t resolve the original issue (creating a new object when pk is set to None), including in multi-inheritance. Therefore, the patch is not correct or complete.
